questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Lifecycle Best Practices”?
options: Lifecycle Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Lifecycle Best Practices means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Lifecycle Best Practices removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Lifecycle Best Practices should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Lifecycle Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Lifecycle Best Practices is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Keeping lifecycle hooks lightweight” under Lifecycle Best Practices. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Lifecycle Best Practices”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
